run_configuration.warm_start: behaviour cloning from per-zone dynamic-programming expert
run_configuration.tariff: Saudi two-tier: 0.18 SAR/kWh up to 6000 kWh/month; 0.30 SAR/kWh above
run_configuration.note: All bills computed from measured kWh via the two-tier tariff, so bill is consistent with energy by construction. Values are means across 3 seeds.

results.note: Peak unchanged (both 9.0 kW): strict band forces compressors on at peak.
Wider band creates legitimate scheduling slack; largest villa saving.
Mild month: little cooling load, looser comfort control (highest mean violation).
Shoulder month: moderate load with diurnal slack; clean comfort.
Near thermal saturation and near the DP physical optimum (~1%): coordination barely helps under strict band at scale.
HIGH SEED VARIANCE (sd 172 SAR). Reported as approximate; needs more seeds. Bill reduction (7.8%) exceeds energy reduction (6.7%) due to Tier-2 avoidance (tariff-crossing effect).

key_findings: Strict-band coordination yields modest savings (1-4%), near the physical optimum for thermally saturated buildings.
Comfort-band extension is the primary lever, roughly tripling villa savings to ~13%.
At building scale, bill reduction can exceed energy reduction because coordination lowers consumption billed at the higher Tier-2 rate.
Peak demand is NOT reduced under a strict band (both controllers peak identically): the comfort constraint forces compressors on at peak.
Savings are larger in shoulder/mild months than in peak July, indicating coordination helps most where cooling demand is substantial but non-saturating.
The 20-zone extended case has high seed variance and is reported as approximate.
